items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: And my first teacher was Rag Baby Stevens.

ctx.x: August the 15th, 1903. My father was a bass drummer in one of the early jazz bands of New Orleans. It was called Fish's Ragtime Military Jazz Band. And my first teacher was Rag Baby Stevens. And my first job was in the carnival parade. In those days the only parade that had any jazz in it at all was the Rex parade, which was a union. The only union parade of all the parades.
How many of those bands would really swing there in the Rex parade?

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: The name of the band that I played with... was called Fishers Ragtime Military Jazz Band... a fellow by the name of Rag Baby Stevens was the snare drummer.

ctx.x: Did they call it jazz then?

Yes. The name of the band that I played with, Doug, is funny. It was called Fishers Ragtime Military Jazz Band. Fishers? My father, my father was a drummer, bass drummer in the band. In those days, they used two drums. My father was the bass drummer, and a fellow by the name of Rag Baby Stevens was the snare drummer. And my father built a harness for me so that I could carry the snare drum. And we made this Rex Parade, which was the big carnival parade even then. And Fishers Band was the only band in the parade…
E-flat clarinet's pretty well disappeared these days.
